stimulus.body: The working note below records the evidence for a claim about how a canvas support changes the drawing. a good answer insists that the support and its weave are part of what the drawing is, and that the marks must be described on that support. questions.stem: Apply “Explain how a support must be accounted for in describing a drawing / The support is part of the drawing. / How a canvas support…” to the four options. Which one is supported?

answer.exemplar: A drawing on a woven support cannot be described as though it were on a smooth one, because the tool meets a grid of high and low points and the stroke is interrupted at every thread. questions.hint: The support is part of the drawing.

answer.exemplar: A later varnish is usually chosen for its clarity and its yellowing, and it fills the fine texture of a dry paint film, which deepens the colour and adds a gloss the artist never applied.
